scientificSummary.scope: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis: immune activation, vascular signalling, fibroblast and matrix responses, skin fibrosis, SSc-ILD and renal crisis. Cross-study synthesis retains culture, observation and trial populations; mixed-subset SSc studies are not diffuse-only evidence. Selected therapies; excludes limited cutaneous phenotype, morphea, overlap syndromes and comprehensive organ/therapy coverage.

paragraphs.text: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis combines immune dysregulation, vascular abnormalities and fibrosis, with heterogeneous organ involvement. In early diffuse disease, anti-topoisomerase I antibodies mark greater interstitial lung disease prevalence, while anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies mark more extensive skin involvement and renal crisis; these associations do not prove antibody causation. Patient immune-complex preparations activated endothelial cultures and altered IL-6, TGF-beta and endothelin responses, with important differences among antibody groups. A complementary innate route links plasmacytoid dendritic cells, CXCL4–DNA complexes and interferon amplification. Effector CD8 T-cell IL-13 production correlates with skin fibrosis. Dermal culture experiments connect IL-6 trans-signalling through STAT3 and TGF-beta/SMAD3 to collagen expression, while IL-13/STAT6 can act independently of TGF-beta1. Early untreated skin studies suggest a macrophage–PDGF/TGF-beta–fibroblast vascular niche, although much of that interaction is inferred from spatial and transcriptomic data. Fibroblast and myofibroblast responses converge on matrix production in skin and lung. Renal crisis represents a vascular and kidney-injury branch, often with hypertension; renin abnormalities alone do not predict it.

This is a cross-study explanation, not a demonstrated universal causal circuit. Cell-culture activity and uncontrolled TGF-beta-blockade biomarkers cannot establish clinical benefit, and skin findings cannot automatically be transferred to lung or kidney. Nintedanib slowed FVC decline in the primary SENSCIS analysis, with missing-data sensitivity and gastrointestinal tolerability limits; skin benefit was not demonstrated. Tocilizumab missed its primary skin endpoint but showed secondary lung-function preservation in selected early inflammatory diffuse disease. Both have verified US adult SSc-ILD indications for slowing pulmonary-function decline. SLS II did not demonstrate mycophenolate superiority over cyclophosphamide; within-arm improvement is not proof of equivalence. ACE inhibitors are guideline-supported at established renal crisis, distinct from prophylaxis, and autologous transplantation has benefits and treatment-related mortality in carefully selected severe diffuse disease. The latter treatments are recorded without claiming SSc-specific regulatory approval. Most sources have abstract-level access; study independence is incompletely established. The IL-13 correction concerns attribution, while the tocilizumab trial has linked corrections requiring further appraisal; current prescribing information independently confirms its indication and overall FVC estimate. Independent scientific review and score calibration remain pending.
